transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jane Alvarez (Redwood AE), Marcus Lin (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CSM); Dr. Elena Park (CTO), Ravi Shah (Lead ML Eng), Sofia Martinez (Platform Ops), Tom Hsu (Finance)

Summary: quick QBR-style review of usage, cost, reliability; dug into dedicated vs hosted, VPC/KMS questions, and agreed on benchmarks and next steps.

00:00 Jane: okay folks, thanks for joining, we're on the top of the hour — welcome to the Lynx Therapeutics quarterly health review. Priya, want to kick off?
00:14 Priya: yeah thanks, quick agenda slide, we want to look at usage and spend since May, highlight any reliability incidents, review your upcoming feature roadmap and then cover the options for private/dedicated footprints.
00:30 Dr. Elena Park: sounds good, we have Ravi and Sofia here because we want clarity on VPC and also the expected cost if we go dedicated. Tom is on for finance questions.
00:46 Jane: great. Marcus will walk through the perf numbers and then we'll get into questions. Marcus over to you.
:01:02 Marcus: cool, thanks. so the headline — traffic up ~2.8x since May, tokens per session increased because of longer clinical summaries, that pushed cost up about 40% month-over-month. I'll share the cost breakdown spreadsheet link after.
01:18 Ravi: that aligns with our observations — more 4k+ prompts per session, sometimes hitting 6k with KV cache reuse.
01:33 Marcus: yeah, worth noting our prefix-KV cache is saving ~18% on tokens for certain flows, but the increased sequence length raises latency. With that profile we see p50 latency at ~210ms on hosted, p95 around 720ms depending on model and batching.
01:48 Sofia: can you clarify "hosted" here — is that our multi-tenant API or our reserved pool?
02:00 Marcus: this is hosted (multi-tenant) numbers; dedicated would reduce variability and get p95 down by ~20-30% in our tests given the same instance type, but costs are higher unless you commit and use reserved capacity.
02:18 Tom: what order of magnitude are we talking for cost delta?
02:26 Marcus: rough rule: dedicated committed pool reduces per-token unit cost by ~15-30% depending on utilization. If you're at high sustained QPS, it rapidly pays back. I'll put concrete numbers in the benchmark doc.
02:44 Dr. Elena Park: and what about quantization — we discussed int8 earlier — will that affect output quality for our clinical extraction tasks?
02:58 Marcus: great question. For our catalog models, some int8/4-bit quantization variants show small regressions on F1 for named entity tasks — usually <2-3% if you're careful. We can run evals on your clinical prompt set. Also, for inference latency it can be a big win.
03:16 Ravi: please do an eval — we can't risk degrading extraction accuracy.
03:22 Marcus: agreed. we'll include quality regression checks in the benchmark plan.
03:35 Jane: switching gears to reliability incidents — Priya, any notable outages?
03:40 Priya: two incidents in July — transient region degradation and a backend cache eviction bug; both were 20–30 minutes, root cause identified, mitigations applied. We've added better tracing hooks and alert thresholds in the console.
03:58 Sofia: did you capture audit logs for those incidents? For compliance we need end-to-end audit trail and access logs.
04:08 Priya: yes, we have audit logs, and we can export logs to your S3/GCS. We'll also provide the SOC 2 attest report and the technical controls doc.
04:20 Sofia: perfect, please send links.

04:36 Marcus: jumping into private deployment questions — when you said private, we mean customer-controlled VPC + private control plane option. That supports KMS integration (bring-your-own-key) and full audit logs. The on-prem package is an option too but is more involved.
04:56 Ravi: for our regulated pipelines we'd prefer VPC with BYOK. Can you confirm key rotation model and whether HSM is supported?
05:08 Marcus: yes BYOK via KMS, rotation supported through standard KMS tooling; we have partner integrations for several HSMs — we'll include the compatibility matrix.
05:20 Dr. Elena Park: what about network egress — can we stop any outbound telemetry beyond control plane?
05:29 Jane: yes there are hardened private options; we can scope the VPC rules so that inference nodes don't have external egress except to the control plane endpoints you approve. We'll put the network diagram in the follow-up.
05:40 Tom: any compliance reviewers we should loop in early?
05:47 Priya: we usually bring in our security engineer and solutions architect for deeper sessions. Also we'll share SOC2 and ISO docs first.

06:02 Marcus: back to economics — I propose we run a short POC: 1) an 8k-context latency and cost benchmark across your top 3 models, 2) an accuracy/regression eval on your prompt sets, 3) a dedicated sizing exercise to recommend reserved units. The benchmark will include sustained and burst scenarios to show utilization sensitivity.
06:26 Ravi: that sounds right. timeline?
06:29 Marcus: I can run the bench and deliver a spreadsheet in one week if you provide prompt samples and traffic profiles.
06:37 Dr. Elena Park: we'll get those to you by Monday. Also, we'd like to see a canary rollout flow — how would you pin a model and roll forward without user disruption?
06:48 Marcus: our rollout supports model pinning, canary percentages, and automatic fallback. You can define route-level policies so critical traffic stays on a pinned model while noncritical traffic moves to the new variant. We'll show a demo in the deep dive.
07:02 Sofia: any tooling to surface regression alerts tied to prompt sets?
07:07 Marcus: yes, Redwood Optimize can connect eval suites to alerts; if a metric falls below threshold, it can auto-notify and even trigger rollbacks. We'll include sample alert configs.

07:18 Tom: budget question again — what's the minimum committed term? 6 months? 12?
07:26 Jane: typically reserved capacity contracts start at 12 months, but we have flexible pilots and short-term burst options. For committed pricing we can model a 12-month vs 24-month scenario.
07:38 Tom: ok we'll evaluate 12 month.

07:45 Dr. Elena Park: any vendor lock-in concerns? We run some workloads on Vertex and internal models.
07:53 Marcus: Redwood focuses on model-agnostic serving — you can host your models or choose curated open models; model export and portability docs will be provided. For dedicated/private the control plane separation reduces lock-in risk.
08:08 Ravi: curious about autoscaling behavior for spikes caused by overnight data ingestion — we need predictable burst capacity.
08:18 Marcus: we offer burst pools and autoscaling policies with predictable cold-start behavior; we can simulate your ingestion spike in the benchmark.
08:30 Sofia: sending the infra diagram now (s3 link) — please confirm receipt.
08:34 Jane: got it, thanks.

08:48 Priya: small note on token-level visibility — we can enable per-token cost breakdowns per route and per model so finance can reconcile invoices.
08:59 Tom: that's helpful. We'll need line-item visibility for audit.
09:06 Jane: we'll include that in the pricing doc.

09:16 Marcus: quick risk points: quantization may introduce minor accuracy drops; VPC/on-prem will increase onboarding time and ops ownership; dedicated has commitment tradeoffs. We'll capture mitigations in the POC plan.
09:34 Dr. Elena Park: agreed. We want the POC to measure both economics and safety.
09:40 Marcus: noted. We'll include regression gates and SLA checks.

09:50 Jane: ok let's summarize next steps before we wrap. Marcus, you'll run the 8k-context benchmarks and share spreadsheet. Priya will send security and SOC2 docs. Jane will send pricing and contract sketch. Customer will provide prompt sets and infra diagram.
10:10 Dr. Elena Park: yes, we'll deliver prompt sets by Monday and confirm budget later this week.
10:20 Jane: great. Any final questions?
10:25 Ravi: one more — can you surface per-model tokenization differences? We saw tokenization blowup on some clinical payloads.
10:33 Marcus: we'll include tokenizer deltas and recommended pre-processing (trimming templates, canonicalization).
10:41 Tom: thanks all.
10:45 Jane: thanks everyone — Priya will follow up with calendar invite for the technical deep dive.
10:52 Priya: sending the invite now.
10:55 Dr. Elena Park: thanks, bye.
10:58 Jane: bye all.

Post-meeting notes:
- Shared artifacts: benchmarking template (link: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/lynx-2027-09), security packet (link: https://redwood.internal/security/lynx-sdcc), infra diagram received (s3://lynx-diagrams/infra-2027-09-14.png)
